newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Absa sees real earnings growth.
newsitem.headline: Absa sees real earnings growth.

text.p: Amalgamated Banks of South Africa Ltd (Absa) said on Monday that it expected real earnings growth in the current year despite continued pressure on net interest margins.

"We look forward to ongoing real growth in earnings through responsible and profitable asset growth and further improvement in the ratio of costs to income," said group chief executive Danie Cronje on the release of year figures.
But Cronje said that the banking group expected its relatively high net interest margins to continue falling to a level of about four percent from 4.28 percent for the year ended March 31, 1997.
Cronje blamed margin pressure mainly on the growth of aggressive niche players and the entry of offshore banks into the South African market.
"We've always had the highest margins of anyone else, so we believe that this is going to be under pressure," he said.
The group, which derives its income mainly from retail deposits, aimed to compensate for interest margin pressure by growing non-interest or fee-related income, he added.
The chief executive said growth in fee income would be targetted through greater cross-selling of insurance and other fee-related activities.
Headline earnings per share totalled 222.2 cents in the year to March against 178.0 in 1995/96.
